item.title: The evolution of tool use in LLM agents: from single-tool call to multi-tool orchestration
item.description: Tool use enables large language models (LLMs) to access external information, invoke software systems, and act in digital environments beyond what can be solved from model parameters alone. item.description: Cybersecurity is changing from reactive, human-centered systems to highly autonomous cyber-capable agents (HACCAs) that can operate at machine speed and scale. item.title: Uncertainty-Guided Counterfactual Sensor Selection and Safety-Gated Recognition for Autonomous Sensing Agents in IoT Systems
item.description: Autonomous IoT systems rely on distributed sensing, but sensor faults and communication loss can leave multichannel evidence incomplete or unreliable. Their agents must therefore classify measurements, assess evidence sufficiency, select a sensor to reacquire, and hand off unsafe decisions. item.description: Genomic analyses such as spatial transcriptomics often generate a large number of candidate targets, but prioritizing targets for functional validation requires expertise across multiple domains and verification across diverse biological resources. item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are a double-edged technology. They can serve as learning assistants in programming while simultaneously raising pedagogical and ethical concerns.
